requirements.notes: Button with data-hovered/pressed/disabled/focus-visible state attributes. Variants are CSS only.
Link component. Underlined by us; the Mangrove host's own links are not, which is a host accessibility finding.
TextField + Label + Input + Text slot=description. aria-describedby wired automatically.
isInvalid + FieldError for the three client-side cases. server-rejected uses Form validationErrors, the documented channel for errors only the server knows; no custom wiring.
isDisabled on Button, TextField and Input.
Select + ListBox, 8 options. Its popover is portalled, so it also needs the token scope class.
Same component, 40 options. Its popover is portalled, so it also needs the token scope class.

Same component, 400 options. Renders all 400 DOM nodes: virtualisation requires wrapping in Virtualizer, which was not used so the comparison stays like-for-like. Its popover is portalled, so it also needs the token scope class.
No single multiselect component exists. Documented pattern is ListBox selectionMode=multiple plus TagGroup/TagList for removable chips, joined by a small onRemove handler.
ComboBox filters as you type at all three sizes with no filter function supplied. Its popover is portalled, so it also needs the token scope class.
DatePicker with per-segment keyboard entry and a Calendar popover. Its popover is portalled, so it also needs the token scope class.

DateRangePicker with granularity="minute" in the free tier. One popover, one focus trap, a single RangeCalendar highlighting the intervening days. This is the requirement that separates candidates: MUI needs two composed pickers because its range components are commercially licensed. Note the hidden form-integration inputs render visibly on this host until the `hidden` attribute is restored -- a Mangrove defect, see EVIDENCE.md. Its popover is portalled, so it also needs the token scope class.

ModalOverlay + Modal + Dialog. Focus trap, Escape dismiss and focus restoration to the trigger all verified by e2e test. Requires the token scope class on the portalled element; see theming.escapeHatchesUsed.
TooltipTrigger is hover AND keyboard-focus triggered by default. Requires the token scope class on the portalled element; see theming.escapeHatchesUsed.
DialogTrigger + Popover, dismiss on outside click, with OverlayArrow. Requires the token scope class on the portalled element; see theming.escapeHatchesUsed.
DisclosureGroup + Disclosure + DisclosurePanel, allowsMultipleExpanded={false} for single-expand without custom state.
React Aria has no card component, correctly: a card is styling, not behaviour. Rendered as plain markup reusing Mangrove's own mg-card classes, so the cost is CSS rather than components.
ListBox selectionMode=single, which supplies roving tabindex and type-ahead that a plain list of links does not.
Table/TableHeader/TableBody/Column/Row/Cell over all 250 rows. Column type formatting uses Intl, driven by the active locale.
Column allowsSorting plus sortDescriptor/onSortChange give the UI, ARIA and keyboard behaviour; the comparator is ours. Handles number, ISO string and locale-aware string.

CORRECTED. selectionMode=multiple gives selection behaviour (click, shift-click, keyboard) but renders NO checkboxes and provides no select-all. The select-all the brief requires only exists once you add a selection column with <Checkbox slot="selection"> in the header and every row: the slot supplies the tri-state and the localised accessible name, the markup and appearance are ours. Originally recorded as native with a select-all that did not exist and that the suite never asserted; found by the delta-react-aria run. Now asserted in e2e.
SearchField supplies the input and its clear affordance; the predicate is ours.
React Aria ships no pagination component at all. Page state, slicing, page-size control and the Previous/Next nav are entirely ours. The clearest gap in the library for this use case.
ResizableTableContainer + ColumnResizer give drag and keyboard resizing. Reorder is not available, but the brief requires either one.
TableBody renderEmptyState is native and ProgressBar covers loading. Error and success banners have no component: they are role=alert and role=status markup we wrote.
Same split: ProgressBar native, banners ours.
RadioGroup + Radio. I18nProvider propagates locale to every component.
I18nProvider with an Arabic locale flips direction for the library's own internals, including date segment order and calendar layout. No custom direction plumbing anywhere.

CORRECTED to clean at all three viewports: 0px horizontal overflow in German at 390, 1024 and 1440. The earlier 261px was two bugs of mine, not a design constraint: a .demo-sbs base rule placed AFTER an equally specific @media block (media queries add no specificity, so the later rule won and the grid stayed two columns at mobile), and ColumnResizer's hidden range input escaping the scroll container for want of a positioned ancestor.

Host and candidate button, table, card and nav list rendered adjacent in section 9. React Aria's button uses the project-owned UNDRR blue family plus Mangrove's square shape, condensed type, spacing and filled secondary treatment. The close visual fit is achievable because every declaration is ours; keeping it synchronized remains bridge ownership rather than inheritance from Mangrove 1.8.1.

theming.method: CSS custom properties from packages/undrr-tokens consumed directly in a scoped stylesheet. React Aria ships no CSS of its own, so there is nothing to override and no specificity contest: components render the class names given to them plus data-* state attributes, which is the documented styling API.
escapeHatchesUsed: One rule targets library-rendered markup: [data-testid="hidden-select-container"] { overflow: hidden } plus a width cap on library-rendered <select> elements. Needed because React Aria's hidden native selects are hidden with clip/clip-path but remain in layout, so a long option label scrolls the whole page sideways. Targeting a data-testid is fragile and would break silently on upgrade.

`.demo [hidden] { display: none }` restores the hidden attribute, which the Mangrove host defeats: its `input[type="text"] { display: block }` rule (0,1,1) outranks its own `[hidden] { display: none }` (0,1,0). Not a candidate problem -- it will affect all four Mangrove pairings.

`.undrr-tokens` is applied to every portalled overlay (Popover, ModalOverlay, Tooltip) via src/overlay-class.ts. React Aria portals overlays to document.body, outside the token-scoped element, so every var(--undrr-*) inside them resolved to nothing: popovers rendered transparent and borderless with the library's inline z-index of 100000. Not a React Aria defect so much as an interaction between portalling and class-scoped tokens, but it is silent -- a failed var() produces no warning.

humanReviewRequired: React Aria renders visually hidden controls that still affect document layout, in two places: ColumnResizer's hidden range input escapes any ancestor overflow unless a positioned ancestor exists, and Select's hidden native <select> stays in layout at its longest-option width. Both silently scroll the page sideways. Worth reporting upstream: a visually hidden control should not be able to change layout.

axe `color-contrast` (1 incomplete, sections 2 and 6): axe could not determine contrast automatically. Needs manual checking, particularly disabled button and hint text against the neutral token palette.
The 400-option Select renders all 400 DOM nodes. Whether that is acceptable, or whether Virtualizer should be mandatory, is a performance decision not taken here.
Keyboard and screen-reader testing by a human. axe is static analysis and cannot confirm that the range calendar, column resizer or listbox type-ahead are usable with a screen reader.

MANGROVE DEFECT, affects all four Mangrove pairings: `input[type=...] { display: block }` outranks `[hidden] { display: none }`, so any library's hidden helper inputs render visibly. Worked around per-app here; should be fixed in Mangrove.
The Mangrove host also contributes a `link-in-text-block` serious violation (whole-page count 1, scoped count 0). Host finding, not a candidate one.

React Aria sets z-index inline on its portal container (100000), which outranks the token z-index scale. The overlay layering tokens are therefore not honoured by this candidate without !important. MUI, whose z-index comes from its theme object, was pinnable to the token scale.
